newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO shuns U.S. call for security ties with Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO shuns U.S. call for security ties with Israel.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority has rejected a U.S. initiative to restore security coordination with Israel, a senior Palestinian security official said on Monday.

Colonel Jibril Rajoub, head of Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, told a news conference that security coordination ended when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers on March 18 to break ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"The Israeli side and the American, through its envoy to the area, Dennis Ross, tried to restore security coordination between the (Palestinian) National Authority and the Israeli side," a press release by the Palestinian Information Ministry, summarising Rajoub's presentation to the press, said.
"But we rejected that and insisted on the linkage between the security coordination and other issues," it quoted him as saying.

Daily clashes between Palestinian protesters and Israeli troops have erupted in the West Bank since the settlement groundbreaking. One Palestinian was killed in a clash on Saturday. A Palestinian suicide bomber killed three women in Tel Aviv on March 21.
Ross met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Netanyahu late last week trying to resolve the crisis.
Rajoub said that security coordination was the product of the 1993 Israeli-PLO peace accord that launched Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

The Palestinian Authority says Israel has violated peace deals by ordering construction of 6,500 housing units for Jews on Jabal Abu Ghneim, a hill of pine trees on the southern outskirts of Jerusalem which Israelis call Har Homa.
Rajoub said there could not be security coordination unless Israel abided by the agreement.
